textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 4 english · The Swing (poem) · Textbook Concepts
textbookBox.concept: The poet asks how you like to go up in a swing, up in the air so blue, and answers that it is the pleasantest thing a child can do.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: The poet asks how you like to go up in a swing, up in the air so blue, and answers that it is the pleasantest thing a child can do.
beats.speakEn: The poet asks how you like to go up in a swing, up in the air so blue, and answers that it is the pleasantest thing a child can do.

beats.en: The poet clearly enjoys swings. The lines saying it is the pleasantest thing a child can do tell us so. The air is called blue because the sky is blue, and the child is swinging high up toward it.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 4 english · The Swing (poem) · Deeper Textbook Ideas
textbookBox.concept: Pleasantest means the most enjoyable. Cattle are farm animals like cows and bulls. Countryside is the land outside towns and cities with fields, villages and farms.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 4 english · The Swing (poem) · Complete Summary
textbookBox.concept: Some words can be a verb in one sentence and a noun in another. I swing on a swing. The first swing is a verb, meaning to move forward and back, and the second is a noun, an object.

beats.en: Let us review the key takeaway from The Swing (poem): Some words can be a verb in one sentence and a noun in another. I swing on a swing. The first swing is a verb, meaning to move forward and back, and the second is a noun, an object.
